La « dame à la lampe » de la guerre de C: The “Lady with the Lamp” of the Crimean War was first of all a statistician. Her diagrams showed that soldiers died more from disease than from wounds, and they got military hospitals reformed.
Autodidacte de Madras, il écrit en 1913: A self-taught man from Madras, in 1913 he wrote to Hardy, at Cambridge, a letter full of astonishing formulas. Hardy visited him in hospital in taxi number 1729, “a rather dull number.” “On the contrary, it is the smallest number expressible as the sum of two cubes in two different ways.”
Il invente la machine qui porte son nom: He invented the machine that bears his name in 1936, broke Enigma during the war and asked the question of thinking machines in 1950. A long-distance runner, he narrowly missed selection for the 1948 Olympic marathon.
En 628, il écrit les premières règles de: In 628, he wrote the first rules for calculating with zero as a number in its own right: a number minus itself gives zero, and the product of two debts is a fortune. He was wrong on only one point: for him, zero divided by zero was zero.
À la Maison de la sagesse de Bagdad, il: At the House of Wisdom in Baghdad, around 820 he wrote a treatise on solving equations by al-jabr, “restoring.” The word gave us “algebra,” and his Latinized name, Algoritmi, gave us “algorithm.” He solved everything in sentences and figures, without a single symbol.
Fils d'un marchand pisan installé à Béja: The son of a Pisan merchant settled in Béjaïa, in Algeria, he learned the Indian numerals there. His Liber abaci (1202) taught merchants the rule of three, interest and currency exchange. The sequence that bears his name is just an exercise about rabbits in it, and Indian mathematicians knew it before him.
À 19 ans, il construit une machine à cal: At 19, he built a calculating machine for his father, a tax collector. In 1654, with Fermat, he invented probability theory to divide the stakes of an interrupted game. Then he applied it to God: that is the wager, where you bet a finite life against an infinite gain.
On ne sait presque rien de lui, sinon qu: Almost nothing is known about him, except that he taught in Alexandria. His Elements is the most copied textbook in history. To King Ptolemy, who wanted a shortcut: “There is no royal road to geometry.” The retort is only reported seven centuries later.
